overview: This single-document file contains a U.S. State Department incoming telegram from Bern reporting a German press account of a Tokyo despatch on impending Japanese railway-fare and postal-rate increases. Effective April 1, 1945, railway tickets were reportedly to rise by 30 percent, producing an anticipated 300 million yen in additional annual receipts, while domestic letter postage would increase from seven to ten sen and postcard postage from three to five sen.

people.name: J. Klahr Huddle
people.role: U.S. diplomatic official in Bern and signatory of the telegram

subfiles.title: Telegram from Bern on Japanese railway and postal rate increases
subfiles.about: Reports a German press account that Japan would raise railway fares and domestic postal charges beginning April 1, 1945.
subfiles.summary: A German press report, citing a Tokyo despatch, states that the Japanese Ministry of Communications had decided to increase railway-ticket prices by 30 percent from April 1, 1945. The increase was expected to yield an additional 300 million yen annually. On the same date, domestic letter postage would rise from seven to ten sen and postcard postage from three to five sen.

interest: The telegram provides concise quantitative evidence of wartime increases in the cost of transportation and communications in Japan during the final months of the Second World War. It is also useful for tracing how information about Japanese domestic economic policy reached the United States indirectly through German press reporting in neutral Bern. The simultaneous increases in railway and postal charges suggest broader fiscal and inflationary pressures on Japan’s state-controlled communications infrastructure.
